newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African gold stocks, virtually ignored in recent weeks, stole the limelight on gains in bullion late on Friday hoisting the all-share index to a fresh record peak and Western Areas up some 16 percent.

Platinum stocks powered ahead, taking the world's biggest producer Rusplats up 3.5 percent to a new 79 rand year high, as the white metal fixed at its highest level since 1990 amid a lack of world supplies.
But industrial stocks, which surged over 230 points this weak following a surprise leap in May official reserves, came off their highs on profit-taking in the afternoon.
"The real turnaround is in bullion. Shares have moved up although the volumes have not been significant," said Dominic Rey, a trader at Investec Securities.
In after-hours trade bullion was changing hands at around $345, some $5 up on its position late on Thursday.
Heavyweight gold stock Vaal Reefs advanced over 2.5 percent to 271.75 rand and Dries was up two percent at 37 rand heaving the all gold index up 35.3 points to 1,175.6.
Dealers said robust gains in platinum stocks, including Amplats which put on over six percent to 34.00 rand could be shortlived if the Russians began supplying the market again.
Amplats managing director Barry Davison told Reuters that there were market rumours that the Russians would resume deliveries during the course of June when their export licences were in place.
"The key question becomes at what rate will they deliver. We have said for some time now that we do believe that the Russian supply for calendar 1997 will be substantially reduced," Davison said.

Dealers said industrial shares also fell back to end only 6.8 points up at 8,476.7 after concerns that Wall Street may open weaker after U.S. jobs data gave conflicting signals about labour market strength.
Local food stock Del Monte slumped almost 14 percent or 45 cents to 280 cents following an earlier warning on a slide in profits at both the half and full year.
But the bank-laced financial index stormed to yet another new peak, up 93.1 points to 9,619.3, on the promise of an easing in pressures on margins if local interest rates were cut.
Absa lifted over 2.6 percent to 29.25 rand and RMB Holdings jumped over three percent to 13.10 rand.
Overall market gains pushed the all-share index to its second consecutive closing high of 7,262.2, a gain of 43.7 points.
Dealers said turnover on the day was slightly below average at around 654 million rand, boosted by modest-sized trades in blue-chips Anglo and Gencor.

The market was seen strong again next week riding on rate cut talk as well as continued foreign and institutional interest. However, analysts said for the rally to continue action was needed on the interest rate front.

"In the very short term the market is looking very strong but the sustainability depends on whether we get a rate cut sooner rather than later," said Piet Viljoen, a portfolio manager at Investec Asset Management.
On the equity index futures market, contracts remained firm on the day with golds taking the lead, wakened from their recent lethargy.
Dealers said the market was expected to become more volatile next week as the June close-out approached.
In late dealings June gold contract was at 833/40 from 800, the industrial contract was at 8,165/75 from 8,151 and the all-share contract was at 6,550/58 from 6,525.
-- Nicole Mordant, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
